The core operator 'association_only_probability' models a single-source probabilistic inference where each game is assigned a scalar likelihood P_assoc ∈ [0,1]. This is derived from a bridge function f_bridge(t_pregame) that maps pregame context to outcome likelihood. The operator assumes no causal structure, only association. When P_assoc > 0.5, it implies a higher likelihood of home win; conversely, P_assoc < 0.5 implies away win. The failure mode occurs when multiple sources exist or when causal mechanisms are known, invalidating the single-source assumption. The GSI mapping applies Bayesian updating with this prior, while GSE uses it to transition states in a belief network. The dual nature of this operator lies in its ability to be both a static measure and a dynamic input to evolving systems. The retrocausal genealogy traces back to classical probability theory and Bayesian inference, particularly in the work of Laplace and Bayes. The theory of mind considers opposing agents who may use different source sets or interpret the same source differently. Anti-collinearity vetoes arise when multiple independent sources are available, as they would contradict the 'association-only' premise.
